biomarkers.name: KRAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very common driver in appendiceal mucinous neoplasms/PMP; supports mucinous appendiceal origin in the appropriate clinicopathologic context but is not specific on its own

biomarkers.name: GNAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: Characteristic alteration in low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm and pseudomyxoma peritonei; supports appendiceal origin in the appropriate context

biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.prevalence: Uncommon in low-grade disease; enriched in high-grade/invasive tumors
biomarkers.clinical_use: TP53 mutation is associated with higher-grade progression and worse outcome

biomarkers.name: Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) — not molecular but standard staging
biomarkers.clinical_use: Guides disease burden assessment and candidacy for cytoreductive surgery ± HIPEC

biomarkers.name: CEA, CA 19-9, CA 125
biomarkers.clinical_use: Commonly used for monitoring in PMP/appendiceal mucinous neoplasms; elevated levels may correlate with tumor burden and prognosis

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Mucinous epithelial neoplasm with pushing invasion; often produces massive extracellular mucin
variants: pseudomyxoma peritonei — low-grade or high-grade subtype based on cellularity + atypia
histomorphological_subtype.grading: PSOGI 2016 terminology for peritoneal disease includes acellular mucin, low-grade mucinous carcinoma peritonei, high-grade mucinous carcinoma peritonei, and high-grade with signet-ring cells; higher grade is associated with substantially worse prognosis

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Immune-cold; peritoneal mucin pools often have minimal immune infiltrate
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Extracellular mucin dominates; often paucicellular peritoneal implants in low-grade PMP

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Appendiceal mucosal epithelium with mucinous differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Well-differentiated mucinous epithelium; pushing borders rather than infiltrative invasion in LAMN, with more overt high-grade cytology in HAMN/high-grade peritoneal disease
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Rupture can disseminate well-differentiated mucin-producing cells throughout the peritoneum, producing pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP); this often reflects redistribution of appendiceal tumor cells rather than acquisition of a new lineage state
